editorial: In "A Haunting in Venice", when the moon rises over the canals, you step into a palazzo that seems to breathe its own secrets. This psychological thriller turns the labyrinthine alleys of Venice into a maze of doubt, where every echo feels as if it were a whisper from beyond. The film’s chiaroscuro lighting turns the rain‑soaked ceilings into a living backdrop, each flicker a reminder of a story left unfinished. The pacing lurches in the middle, letting tension simmer a bit too long before jolting back into motion. You will be drawn in if you appreciate atmospheric dread that lingers longer than the last breath.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy atmospheric dread over conventional scares.
